scope: Economy checked-bag weight, overweight bands and fees, over-maximum rule, size limits, cabin bag and personal item for the carriers on SLATE's markets (New York, Los Angeles, New Haven, London, Dublin, Toronto, Vancouver, Mexico City); typical garment weights; the cabin liquids rules. Read for src/engine/content/air.ts, which today prices a flat $45 checked bag on US carriers and includes one across oceans, with no weight limit at all.

commonRule.text: Across every full-service carrier read, the standard economy checked bag is 23 kg / 50 lb and 158 cm / 62 in linear (length + width + height). A bag over that weight up to 32 kg / 70 lb pays an overweight fee per bag per direction; 32 kg / 70 lb is the most any carrier read accepts on transatlantic and Canadian/European routes, and above it the bag must go as cargo or be repacked. Fees are cumulative: Delta's own page says there are separate fees for each limitation exceeded (size, weight, number).
commonRule.note: The 32 kg ceiling comes from airport/ground-handling manual-handling limits; on US domestic flights Delta, United and American accept up to 100 lb / 45 kg for a higher fee, and Volaris to 45 kg.

garmentWeights.basis: Dry weights from laundry-load tables. No appliance maker publishes a per-garment table that could be read; Beko's own load guide gives only '7 kg is about 35 shirts' (=200 g a shirt). The tables below are a laundromat chain's (Speed Queen franchise, France) and a UK laundry site's, both secondhand. Use the midpoint unless a garment's fabric is known.

shirtBlouse.note: Beko: 7 kg load about 35 shirts = 200 g each

trousers.note: cotton/chinos; inthewash smart trousers women's 400, men's 650

suit.note: two-piece; merino 0.9-1.4 kg, tweed 1.8-2.7 kg. No laundry table lists a suit.

jacketCoat.note: inthewash light jacket women's 1200, men's 2000 (looks high)

shoesPair.note: men's dress shoes; trainers 600 women's / 900 men's per inthewash

toiletries.rule: A water-based liquid, gel or cream weighs about 1 g per ml (water's density is 1.000 g/ml at 4 C; most toiletries are 0.9-1.1). A 100 ml bottle is therefore about 100 g of contents plus its container.
toiletries.derivation: Physical density of water; container weights below are estimates of typical plastic travel packaging, not a published table.

typicalPackedWashBag.derivation: empty bag + toothbrush + toothpaste + deodorant + razor + three or four 100 ml bottles

inthewash.note: cites no source; says figures are averages

beko.status: secondhand (via search summary; 7 kg = about 35 shirts)

US.rule: TSA 3-1-1: liquids, aerosols, gels, creams and pastes in travel-size containers of 3.4 oz / 100 ml or less each, all in one quart-size bag, one bag per passenger.
US.overLimit: Containers over 3.4 oz / 100 ml must go in checked baggage; at the checkpoint an over-size container is surrendered (discarded) or taken back to check in. Anything that alarms gets extra screening.
US.exemptions: Medically necessary liquids, baby formula/breast milk in reasonable quantities, declared at the checkpoint.

UK.rule: Default (GOV.UK): containers of at most 100 ml, in one transparent resealable bag holding no more than 1 litre (about 20 x 20 cm), one per person, where the airport requires the bag. GOV.UK says some airports allow containers up to 2 litres and tells travellers to check their departure and connecting airports.

byAirport.asOf: August 2026 per secondhand summaries; Which? (as of January 2026) listed the same 2-litre airports less Bournemouth

UK.history: The 100 ml rule dates from 2006. New CT scanners let some airports lift it in 2024; on 14 June 2024 the DfT reimposed 100 ml at all UK airports as a temporary measure; airports then lifted it one by one from 2025 as their scanners were approved. At 2-litre airports liquids may stay in the bag and electronics need not come out.
UK.historyStatus: secondhand (dates from general reporting, not re-read this pass)
UK.overLimit: An over-limit container is surrendered at security; frozen liquids are not allowed in hand luggage at any UK airport. Exemptions up to 2 litres: essential medicines, special dietary foods, baby food/milk. Sealed duty-free bags with receipt allowed.
UK.connectionRule: The return or connecting airport's rule governs: a 2-litre bottle accepted at Heathrow can be refused flying home from a 100 ml airport such as Manchester.
UK.status: verified (GOV.UK default rule and exemptions); secondhand (airport list)

EU_Ireland_Canada_Mexico.rule: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag remain the default at Dublin, Canadian (CATSA) and Mexican airports; EU airports with approved CT scanners (Dublin among them in 2024) were also pulled back to 100 ml by the EU in 2024. Current Dublin state not re-read in this pass.
